questions.question: In the context of a severe allergic reaction, how do clinicians differentiate between biphasic anaphylaxis and refractory anaphylaxis?

The patient in this case initially received 0.3 mg of epinephrine via an auto-injector. For an adult weighing over 50 kg, what is the standard recommended dose, and what clinical evidence suggests that the 0.3 mg dose may be suboptimal?

Corticosteroids were administered to this patient to prevent the recurrence of symptoms. Based on recent systematic reviews and contemporary guidelines, what is the current consensus on the efficacy of corticosteroids in preventing biphasic anaphylaxis?
To accurately diagnose anaphylaxis and evaluate for underlying mast cell disorders, what is the recommended timing and sequence for collecting serum tryptase samples?
This patient showed evidence suggestive of systemic mastocytosis. Pathophysiologically, how does systemic mastocytosis predispose an individual to more severe or atypical anaphylactic courses?

When managing a patient after the initial resolution of anaphylaxis, what are the proposed clinical predictors for a biphasic reaction, and why is the optimal observation window still a subject of debate?
